<div class="modal-body " style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);"><p style="overflow-wrap: break-word;">Officers received objection comments from the neighbour of the adjoining property stating that the extension is excessively high thus has significantly reduced the natural light to their property as well as appearing overbearing and out of keeping with neighbouring properties. Subsequently, officers attempted to contact the applicant to arrange a site visit multiple times between 9th June to 1st July however, they received no response with regards to arranging a site visit. Given the neighbour's objections comments, officers considered a site visit to be fundamental to their decision making to determine whether the height of the rear extension aligns with the height indicated on the proposed plans. Therefore, having not been able to arrange a visit to the site, officers cannot determine that the extension is acceptable with regards to design and neighbouring amenity.&nbsp; As such, the development is likely to be contrary to: - National Planning Policy Framework &nbsp;(NPPF) (December 2024) - Polies D1, D4, D5 and D6 of the London Plan (March 2021) -&nbsp; Policies&nbsp; DMD1, DMD5 and&nbsp; SP2 of&nbsp; the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan (September 2024) - The Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (February 2012)</p></div>
